name: Social Anxiety
description: Intense fear or anxiety in social situations involving scrutiny by others, such as meeting people, performing, speaking up, or being watched while doing everyday things.

immediateActions.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Social Grounding
instructions: While in the anxious moment, discreetly do this silently to come back to present: Name 5 things you can SEE
Name 4 things you can physically TOUCH (clothes on skin, feet on floor, chair under you)
Name 3 things you can HEAR right now
Name 2 things you can SMELL (even if just your shampoo or room air)
Name 1 thing you can TASTE (mouthwash, toothpaste, drink)
Remind yourself: I am safe. My body is having a feeling. This feeling will pass. I have gotten through this before.

immediateActions.title: Conversation Safety Script
instructions: Before entering the situation, write down 3 safe, open-ended questions: How's your week been? Seen anything good lately? Working on anything fun?
Write down 2 safe responses for yourself: I agree completely / That sounds really interesting / Tell me more about that
Write 1 graceful exit line: It was so good catching up, I need to go grab a drink / check on something, I'll be around later!
Read through your script once and fold it away — just knowing it's there will reduce uncertainty
Remember: most people are thinking about themselves, not judging you — that is the quiet truth of most social moments

immediateActions.title: Anxiety Labelling & Normalising
instructions:
Say silently or on paper, finish these sentences:
I am feeling _________ (name the exact feeling: nervous, exposed, judged, hot, tight)
This feeling makes me want to _________ (escape, hide, leave, freeze)
I have felt this way before and I got through it: TRUE / FALSE
The most likely outcome of this situation is _________ (not the worst case, the realistic case)
One kind thing I can tell myself right now is: _________
Now take 3 slow box breaths and choose your next small step

safetyGuidance: Social anxiety is one of the most common and most treatable anxiety conditions — you are far from alone in this. Evidence-based approaches like CBT and graded exposure have strong success rates. If social anxiety is significantly limiting your life, please consider working with a CBT-specialised therapist. There is a version of you that can move through the world with greater ease, and that version is absolutely reachable with support and practice.
